subject.title: ci: harden HTTP and local-auth gates against transient failures

question: Should the remaining CI hardening be owned as one reliability effort, or split into runner-capacity verification, HTTP-fixture failure classification, and local-auth retry/query-load changes?
rationale: The remaining work crosses external runner provisioning, test-fixture semantics, and browser/Convex load behavior; choosing the boundary determines what may safely retry and which failures must remain immediately visible.

options.title: Split by failure boundary
options.body: Keep the current runner diagnostics, then track bounded GitHub-fixture retry and local-auth readiness/query work as separate scoped changes with their own proof.

options.title: Own one CI reliability initiative
options.body: Assign one owner to land a coordinated workflow, fixture, and helper redesign with repeated-run evidence across all affected shards.

options.title: Treat capacity as sufficient for now
options.body: Accept the runner upgrade as the only change and leave the live-fixture and retry behavior unchanged, with continued exposure to unrelated-gate flakes.

recommendation.title: Split by failure boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the current runner diagnostics, then track bounded GitHub-fixture retry and local-auth readiness/query work as separate scoped changes with their own proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged CI reliability work makes this the best available routing candidate for the workflow-level scope decision.
